description: Unlawful presence over 180 days triggers a 3-year bar; over a year, a 10-year bar. But the bar attaches on departure. Staying silently accrues no penalty you ever have to face; leaving to regularise is what activates it.
energy_note: Doing it properly is what gets you barred.

aspect: Which is why the consulate is in Ciudad Juárez
description: Immigrant visa interviews for Mexican applicants are consolidated at Ciudad Juárez. A man who has lived in Chicago for fifteen years must travel to a border city he may never have seen, to be interviewed, and may simply not be allowed back.
energy_note: Flown to a city he does not know, to find out if his life continues.

aspect: The waiver exists and is discretionary
description: The I-601A provisional waiver lets some applicants seek forgiveness of the bar before departing, on proof of extreme hardship to a qualifying US relative. Hardship to himself does not count, and 'extreme' is not defined by a number.
energy_note: His own ruin is not a qualifying hardship.

description: The word people use for it is *el castigo* - the punishment. His lawyer said it was the right thing to do. He is thirty-eight, his children are in Illinois, and a man behind glass in Juárez has just told him ten years. He asks whether there is an appeal. There is not.
energy_note: Ten years, said through glass, with no appeal.
